title: Closed fibres are empty or singleton under point separation
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be a scheme over $k$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that distinct closed points of $X$ have distinct images under $f$. For every closed point $p\in Y$ [def-weil-closed-points], the fibre $f^{-1}(p)$ is either empty or the singleton set $\{x\}$ for one closed point $x\in X$.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, proof after condition (1), with Tag 0478 for closed points in closures

proof.text: By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], X is Jacobson. For a closed point p of Y, its fibre F is closed by continuity. If F is empty, take the first alternative. Otherwise the Jacobson property gives a point x in F which is closed in X (Mathlib nonempty_inter_closedPoints).

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, the small detail after injectivity on closed points, using Tag 0478(2)

proof.text: The intersection F with the closed points of X equals {x}: it contains x, and any other point y in the intersection has f(y)=p=f(x), so injectivity on closed points gives y=x.

source.place: Tag 0E8S, lemma-separate-points-tangent-vectors, the small detail after injectivity on closed points, using Tag 0478(2)

proof.text: By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], F is the closure of its intersection with the closed points (the class field closure_inter_closedPoints). Step 2 identifies that intersection with {x}, whose closure is itself because x is closed. Thus F={x}, with x closed in X, proving the second alternative.

split_report.summary: Split the closed-fibre argument into existence of a closed point and uniqueness. A nonclosed point in a fibre would have infinitely many closed specializations by the existing finite-type closure node; closedness of the fibre puts them in the same fibre, contradicting injectivity on closed points. No new nodes were needed.
